Drake is married to Brenda Drake. An alumna of [Stanford](/wiki/Stanford "Stanford") and [Berkeley Law](/wiki/Berkeley_Law "Berkeley Law"), Brenda Drake is an attorney and has served as a director or trustee of organizations focused on education, international health, finance, civil rights and the arts, including the [National Urban League](/wiki/National_Urban_League "National Urban League"), City Arts & Lectures in San Francisco, [San Francisco University High School](/wiki/San_Francisco_University_High_School "San Francisco University High School") and Golden Gate Bank.[[18]](#cite_note-18) She is a director emerita and former board chair of Engender Health Inc., an international women's health organization, and is currently a trustee of the [Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive](/wiki/Berkeley_Art_Museum_and_Pacific_Film_Archive "Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive").[[19]](#cite_note-19)[[20]](#cite_note-20) Drake and his wife have two adult sons and four grandchildren.

Drake's first job was working at [Tower Records](/wiki/Tower_Records "Tower Records"). He is quoted as saying he has a "passion for music, which is still a hobby today".[[21]](#cite_note-21) In 2015, Drake was appointed to the board of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum, Inc. He has had a lifelong interest in music (notably rock and jazz), plays guitar, and teaches an undergraduate course on the music of the civil rights movement.[[22]](#cite_note-RockAndRollMuseum-22)

* In 2017, he and his wife, Brenda, were awarded the 10th Annual King Arts Legends & Legacies Award as well as the University of California-Irvine Medal, joining past honorees ranging from U.S. presidents to Ella Fitzgerald.[[23]](#cite_note-:1-23)

University of Greifswald :: Organisation :: Central governance :: chunk_0007
The Rectorate, consisting of the [rector](/wiki/Rector_(academia) "Rector (academia)"), three pro-rectors, and the registrar, represents the university as a whole, sets the main guidelines development, distributes the finances, opens and closes study programmes, and appoints professors.[[18]](#cite_note-18) The registrar is the head of the university administration, and manages the university's budget. The rector is elected by the Senate for a four-year term, the registrar for an eight-year term, and the three pro-rectors are elected to serve for two years.

The Senate is the second governing institution of the university.[[19]](#cite_note-19) The Senate elects the Rectorate, and is itself elected by the members of the university, i.e. by students and members of staff. Senators serve for two years, student senators for one year. The Senate consists of academic staff members (divided into professors and non-professors), students, and non-academic staff members (librarians, administration officials, etc.).

Moreover, there is a University Council (*Universitätsrat*), consisting of six prominent members of the public who are elected by the Senate to advise the university in various ways.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

Gina Marie Raimondo was born in 1971[[17]](#cite_note-17) in [Smithfield, Rhode Island](/wiki/Smithfield,_Rhode_Island "Smithfield, Rhode Island"), where she later grew up. He increased the number of [American military advisers](/wiki/Military_advisor#US_advisors_in_Vietnam "Military advisor") in [South Vietnam](/wiki/South_Vietnam "South Vietnam"), and the [Strategic Hamlet Program](/wiki/Strategic_Hamlet_Program "Strategic Hamlet Program") began during his presidency. In 1961, he authorized attempts to overthrow the Cuban government of [Fidel Castro](/wiki/Fidel_Castro "Fidel Castro") in the failed [Bay of Pigs Invasion](/wiki/Bay_of_Pigs_Invasion "Bay of Pigs Invasion") and [Operation Mongoose](/wiki/Operation_Mongoose "Operation Mongoose"). In October 1962, U.S. spy planes discovered Soviet missile bases had been deployed in Cuba. The resulting period of tensions, termed the [Cuban Missile Crisis](/wiki/Cuban_Missile_Crisis "Cuban Missile Crisis"), nearly resulted in [nuclear war](/wiki/Nuclear_war "Nuclear war"). In August 1961, after [East German](/wiki/East_Germany "East Germany") troops erected the [Berlin Wall](/wiki/Berlin_Wall "Berlin Wall"), Kennedy sent an army convoy to reassure West Berliners of U.S. support, and delivered [one of his most famous speeches](/wiki/Ich_bin_ein_Berliner "Ich bin ein Berliner") in West Berlin in June 1963. In 1963, Kennedy signed the first [nuclear weapons treaty](/wiki/Partial_Nuclear_Test_Ban_Treaty "Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty"). He presided over the establishment of the [Peace Corps](/wiki/Peace_Corps "Peace Corps"), [Alliance for Progress](/wiki/Alliance_for_Progress "Alliance for Progress") with Latin America, and the continuation of the [Apollo program](/wiki/Apollo_program "Apollo program") with the goal of [landing a man on the Moon](/wiki/We_choose_to_go_to_the_Moon "We choose to go to the Moon") before 1970. The Grammy Award for Best Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media was announced on June 9, 2022 alongside four additional new categories that would be presented for the first time at the [65th Annual Grammy Awards](/wiki/65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "65th Annual Grammy Awards").
